MASONIC HISTORICAL SITES
(1)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F. & A. M. of California:

WHEREAS, with the passage of time the opportunity for the acquisition, restoration and preservation of significant and important Masonic historical sites
becomes less possible as such sites deteriorate, are destroyed or become
unavailable due to other usage, and
WHEREAS, with the same passage of time the importance and value of
preservation of much that remains to remind us of our Masonic heritage is
increasingly important, and
WHEREAS, the Grand Lodge of California, despite some significant accomplishments of historical site preservation, such as the Masonic Temple at Columbia and the Old Masonic Hall at Los Angeles, has no clear policy with respect
to the acquisition, restoration and preservation of Masonic historical sites, and
WHEREAS, without the establishment of policy valuable time and opportunity may be forever lost,
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that the policy of the Grand
Lodge of California for the acquisition, restoration and preservation of Masonic
Historical Sites be as follows:
1. The Grand Lodge of California desires to restore and preserve, whenever
possible, buildings and related sites which have important historical
significance to Freemasonry and which will portray to present and future
generations examples and reminders of our heritage, both as to important
events and fraternal environment.
2. Whenever possible, preserved structures and memorial markers should be
on public land, which land has been designated for permanent care and
responsibility, or upon land that the owner has conveyed to a Masonic
Body or governmental entity, with a binding, written agreement that the
site be dedicated to such use in perpetuity.
3. There can be no fixed set of guidelines or requirements relative to the
acquisition, restoration or preservation of Masonic Historical Sites. Each

208

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

proposal must be considered on the merit of the known facts of the
present and probable future situation of the site and its relationship to the
heritagef purposes of Freemasonry in California.
4. The restoration and preservation of Masonic buildings should be with
agreements that contemplate occasional usage for Masonic purposes as
well as for public or exhibition purposes.
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Grand Lodge Committee on Masonic History shall receive and study all proposals for Masonic historical site
preservation or designation which are contemplated for accomplishment by. the
Grand Lodge of California. If a proposed project is determined by the Comrmttee
on Masonic History to be appropriate and desirable for accomplishmen~ by the
Grand Lodge, it shall then be submitted to the Grand Lodge Committee on
Finance for its approval with respect to attendant financial obligation involving
funds of the Grand Lodge, either existing funds or funds to be acquired. Following approval by the Grand Lodge Committees on Masonic History and on
Finance, the proposed project shall be submitted to the Grand Lodge for
acceptance by the Grand Lodge at the next Annual Communication. It shall be
permissible for proponents of a proposed project which h.as been ap~roved.by the
Grand Lodge Committees on Masonic History and on Fmance to crrcularize the
Lodges of the Jurisdiction with a written description and explanation of the
project, such circular being frrst approved as to form and content by the Grand
Lodge Committee on Masonic History.
Respectfully submitted,

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 3 attempts to amend our California Masonic Code,
particularly annotation (c) of Section 150, with regard to changing the
requirements for a Mason to become eligible for a Veterans Button or fifty year
pin.
While this Committee can sympathize with the Brother proposing the resolution and with the Brother whom it is intended to help, nevertheless a special
exception is created by it directed to one individual which is contrary to the
policies of this Grand Lodge. Special situation resolutions defeat the purpose
intended by our governing Masonic law.
As our Code presently reads, the criteria for eligibility to receive a Veteran's
Button is set forth and firmly established over many years.
If the only reqvirement is that a Mason is eligible fifty years after he is raised,
as, in effect, called for by the proponent of this resolution, the rewarding of a
Mason for long and faithful support and services is defeated. Under this resolution a Mason who has been suspended for almost a full fifty years could be
eligible. This would be repugnant to the intent of the Veterans Button.
We move the adoption of the resolution, but recommend a "No" vote.
The Committee on Jurisprudence:
This resolution provides that a Lodge, by unanimous ballot taken in the same
manner required for balloting on applicants for Degrees under Section 536 of the
California Masonic Code, may apply to the Grand Master, with recommendation
of the Grand-Secretary, for a dispensation to present a Veteran's Button to a Mason who has been a Master Mason for fifty years, but not in good standing for the
fifty years as presently required under Section 150-C of the Code; and authorizes
the Grand Master to issue a dispensation therefore.
In order. to carry out the intent of the proponent, the Committee on
Jurisprudence offers the following:
·

follows:

(4)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:
WHEREAS, in an effort to establish a uniform system of Ritual in the Grand
isdi9tion of California, it was determined at the Annual Communication of
1873 that all Inspectors would be required to attend Grand Lodge, and with the
Grand Lecturer examine the work and exemplify it before Grand Lodge; then in
1908, the Grand Lecturer's Annual School of Instruction for Inspectors at each
Annual Communication was established and became part of Masonic law by
insertion into the Grand Lodge Constitution of 1910, and
WHEREAS, through the years the Grand Lecturer's school at Grand Lodge
was the only school held by the Gr'and Lecturer for the Inspectors, and was therefore essential in maintaining uniformity in the Ritual, and
WHEREAS, the Inspectors' Annual Spring Conferences were instituted in
1948, a system whereby the Grand Lecturer and the entire Ritual Committee,
each year in early spring, travel to each of the Divisions and spend an entire
weekend reviewing the Ritual and discussing matters of administration, and
WHEREAS, the Inspectors' Spring Conferek have proven to be of great
value as a means of instructing the Ritual, not only because there is sufficient
time to cover all phases of the Ritual, but also assures a more efficient flow of
information within the instructional chain through closer personal contact between the Inspectors and members of the Ritual Committee, and
WHEREAS, the instruction of the Ritual is being more than adequately covered at the Inspectors' Spring Conferences, it is felt that the Grand Lecturer's
Annual School at Grand Lodge could now be discontinued with no resultant loss
of Ritual proficiency, and further, such a move would result in a rather
substantial savings to the Grand Lodge.

Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence, on Policy and General
Purposes and on Finance.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
This resolution proposes to eliminate the Lodge of Instruction for the
Inspectors held at each Annual Communication of the Grand Lodge.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes is well aware of the renown
enjoyed by the Grand Lodge of California because of the excellence of its ritual
•
work.
Your Committee concurs with the proponents of the resolution in their
statement' 'the instruction of the Ritual is being more than adequately covered at
the Inspectors' Spring Conferences."
Furthermore, we are assured adequate instruction in Administration can be
provided at the respective Assistant Grand Lecturers' Schools of Instruction. Additional valuable instruction in Administration is provided in the Manuals available to eachptor.
We are also aware of the substantial monetary savings which will result from
this proposal.
The adoption of this resolution will not preclude the attendance of Inspectors
at the Grand Lodge Communication, at the request of the Grand Master, and
their being reimbursed therefor.
The Grand Lecturer and the entire Ritual Committee propose and support the
resolution. Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes concurs and recommends a "yes" vote.
I move the adoption of Resolution No. 4.

The Committee expressed its concurrence with the recommendation of the
Committee on Policy and General Purposes.

This resolution seeks to amend Section 252 of the California Masomc Code
relating to appointment of Grand Lodge Officers, namely the Deputy Grand
Master, Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer to the California Masonic
Foundation.
.
.
..
,,
At the present time the Code Section makes it mandatory with the word shall
that they be members of the Board.
As the California Masonic Foundation is a "Private Foundation" under the tax
rules of the Federal Internal Revenue Code it enjoys considerable tax advantages.
However, with the present wording of a portion of Section 252 an improper supervisory provision is imposed by making certain Grand Lodge Officers mandatory
Trustees, all of which may violate the Internal Revenue Act.
The amendment proposed would change "shall" to "may" with regard to ~he
appointment of the Deputy Grand Master to the Board of Trustees, thus removmg
the mandatory provisions. Finally, the proposed amendments would remove the
restriction that the Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer shall always be Secretary
and Treasurer for the Board of Trustees.

Committee on Taxation :
The California Masonic Foundation was organized March 5, 1969 as a non
profit, charitable corporation. The foundation is managed by fifteen trustees all of
whom must be members of Grand Lodge one of whom is the Deputy Grand Master
and the other fourteen are appointed by the Grand Master for staggered terms of
three years each. The Grand Secretary is the Secretary of the Board of Trustees and
the Grand Treasurer is the Treasurer of the Board of Trustees. The Grand Lodge
office performs the accounting for the Foundation without charge. The Grand
Lodge Committee on Investments is empowered to invest and reinvest the funds of
the Foundation . The assets of the Foundation originated by gifts from the Grand
Lodge and the Order of the Amaranth.
The Committee on Taxation has had referred to it Resolution #5 of the 1974
Annual Communication . The resolution proposes certain changes in the California
Masonic Code having to do with the appointment of the Deputy Grand Master and
Grand Secretary and Grand Treasurer and with the removal of trustees. The reason
for the changes is given as possible violations of the Internal Revenue Code.
The Committee on Taxation will not comment on the matter of policy in regard
to this resolution . Its comments are limited to the reference to the Internal Revenue
Code. It further will not comment on the tax status of the Foundation beyond the
subject of the resolution.
The Committee on Taxation does not believe the changes proposed by the resolution are necessary to avoid violation of the Internal Revenue Code and the resolution should not be approved on that basis alone.
The Committee on Taxation understands that the California Masonic Foundation has received exempt status from the Internal Revenue Service as organized for
charitable and educational purposes (Section 501 (c) (3)) .
The Committee further understands that the Foundation has been classified by
the Internal Revenue Service as a privately supported organization-a private
foundation . A private foundation is defined (Section 509 (a)) as an organization
which is not a publicly supported organization by virtue of its failure to meet certain specified criteria enumerated in the code (Section 509 (a) (1), (2), (3), or (4)).
It should be observed that were the Foundation not classified as a private foundation it could still qualify with exempt status-a public foundation (Section 501 (c)
(3)) . Such classification would be advantageous in the avoidance of the excise tax
to which the foundation is subject.
The Internal Revenue Code generally prohibits donor-foundation financial
transactions . The prohibited transactions or "acts of self-dealing" generally
include any direct or indirect transactions between a private foundation and its do-

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

217

not or related parties referred to as disqualified persons involving the transfer or
use of the foundation assets (Section 4941).
It appears that the Foundation and all of its trustees are disqualified persons
(Section 4946 (a) (1). The Deputy Grand Master, the Grand Secretary, and the
Grand Treasurer appear no more disqualified than any other trustees all of whom
are appointed by the major donor-the Grand Lodge.
If the trustees are all disqualified persons, it is then essential that no prohibited
acts of self-dealing occur between a disqualified person and the private foundation
(Section 4941 (d)). Self-dealing would generally be a transaction giving
advantages to Grand Lodge. It does not appear that the operation of the California
Masonic Foundation would at any time involve self-dealing, however the Trustees
should be aware of the prohibited acts .
Resolution # 5 does not appear necessary or to be of assistance in changing the
Foundation's status regarding self-dealing of disqualified persons. The Committee
on Taxation cannot determine that Resolution# 5 requires adoption based on the Internal Revenue Code.
The Trustees of the Foundation are to be commended for their attention to the
requirements of the Internal Revenue Code . Private foundations are subject to
complex laws and regulations and our Foundation must comply with the laws .
Adopted

The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes is in sympathy with the
search by Lodges for additional revenues. Those Lodges having investment in
owned or leased buildings wherein facilities sufficiently separated from the
Lodge Room may be rented to individuals or groups for non-Masonic social,
commercial or other lawful events seek authority to permit renters to serve champagne, light wines and beer at such events.
It is difficult to perceive any way in which moderation in the use of alcoholic
beverages could be controlled and assured and the reference to " strict supervision of the Grand Lodge or Inspectors'' to prevent excess appears to the Committee to be unreasonably optimistic.
Each of us has been charged upon becoming a Master Mason to "preserve unsullied the reputation of the Fraternity ." By providing Masonic facilities for nonMasonic events at which the stimulus of intoxicants might lead to some of those
in attendance becoming noisy or unruly could certainly result in the conclusion in
the minds of neighboring residents or passers-by that Masons did not entirely obserVe the limits of good conduct.
I move adoption of Resolution No. 6 and your Committee on Policy and
General Purposes recommends a "No" vote.

Grand Lecturer's Statement - Flag Ceremony:
Regarding the present ceremony of receiving the Flag of the United States in
our Lodges, I have the following comment:

220

221

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

This Ceremony as now taught by the Grand Lecturer specifies that the Flag of
our Country shall be received in the manner clearly outlined in our Officers'
Manual and Monitor pages 53 through 54.
As regards Masonic Law, it is required that the American Flag be presented at
the Altar and received according to proper form at the annual election of officers,
and at such other meetings as may be deemed appropriate by the Master of the
Lodge. In other words, other than one time each year at the annual election of officers , it is entirely optional whether the Flag shall be presented at the Altar.
Grand Lecturers in the past have adopted the policy that if the option is exercised
to present the Flag of the United States at any meeting, then it must also be retired in the manner prescribed in the Monitor pages 55-56.
Also, ifthe Flag is received and retired , then it becomes a requirement that the
Brethren sing one chorus of America, or the Star Spangled Banner.
There is presently much objection to the Brethren being required to sing as the
Flag is retired, and having suffered through some extremely discordant examples
of such singing, this Grand Lecturer is just as opposed to this practice as are the
Brethren.
After thorough discussion of this situation with several of the Brethren, and
the entire Ritual Committee being in full accord , I now wish to state that henceforth the Grand Lecturer shall teach a new policy regarding the reception of the
Flag and that policy shall be as follows:
If the Lodge determines to present the Flag at a meeting other than the
required annual election meeting, they may do so in accordance with the provisions set forth in the Officers' Monitor.
They will not be required to officially retire the Flag, however, unless the
Master of the Lodge should so desire: and, further, I recommend that it become
policy of this Grand Lodge that singing America or the Star Spangled Banner at
retirement of the Flag be optional to the Master of the Lodge.

Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence and on Policy and General
Purposes:
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolution No. 9 seeks to amend Article II, Section 1, of the Uniform Code of
By-Laws of Lodges so as to clarify the appointment of the Junior Deacon.
The concerned section confers absolute power to the Master for the
appointment of officers for the Lodge other than the elected officers as set forth
in Section 471 of the Ordinances of Grand Lodge. It does not vest the Senior
Warden with the exclusive right to make such appointment but rather permits
him to exercise his prerogative to appoint the Junior Deacon with the approval of
the Master.
The resolution as proposed does not change the purpose and intent of Section
1 of the Uniform Code of By-Laws of Lodges and its adoption would not accomplish the purpose intended by the proponent of the resolution.
I move the adoption of the resolution and the Committee on Policy and
General Purposes recommends a "No" vote.
The Committee on Jurisprudence:
Your Committee on Jurisprudence, to which has been referred Resolution No.
9, reports as follows:
The Resolution requires that Section 342 be amended.
The alternative form of the Resolution as propounded creates an ambiguity as
to whether it is intended thereby to give the Master discretion to allow the Senior
Warden to appoint the Junior Deacon. The propounder of the Resolution has
informed your Committee that his intent is to propose that the phrase ''except the
Junior Deacon, who may be appointed by the Senior Warden," be deleted.
Therefore, to carry out the intent of the proponent, we submit the following
legislation:
''RESOLVED, that Section 342' of the California Masonic Code be amended
by deleting from the second sentence thereof the words 'except the Junior Deacon, who may be appointed by the Senior Warden,' so that such sentence shall
read as follows:
''The other officers shall be appointed by the Master.''
We move adoption of this Resolution without recommendation.
Adopted 5/6 vote.

receipted vouchers."

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:

York Rite Bodies) is also a fact.

from the form of the Application for the Degrees of Masonry in Section 527 of
the California Masonic Code, that Question No. 16 be renumbered No. 15, and
that Annotations 527a, 527b, 527c, 527d, 527f, 527h and 527i, be deleted from
the California Masonic Code.

Application for the Degrees of Masonry will permit the encouragement of newly

concordant bodies, requiring only a satisfactory examination in the lecture of the
Master Mason Degree. That Question No. 15 on the application blank for the
degrees serves no particular purpose in Masonry, and should be deleted for the
reason as set forth in this paragraph.

D.L. CHAMPLIN, P.M., No.
Referred to the Committies on Jurisprudence and on Policy and General
Purposes.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
Resolutions No . 11 and 12 both propose a revision to Section 527 of the
Comia Masonic Code which specifies the form of application for Degrees in
Masonry. Both resolutions address themselves to amending Question 15 of the
application form.
In applying for the Degrees of Masonry, the Candidate must answer affirmatively Question 15 which states "Do you promise that you will not apply
for or receive any Degree or be initiated in any Lodge, Order or organization, the
prerequisite of membership wherein is that a person be a Master Mason, until
you have given satisfactory evidence, by strict examination in open Lodge, that
you are entirely proficient and well-qualified in the Candidate's Lecture of the
Degree of Master Mason and in no event within twelve months after you have
received the Degree of Master Mason?"
Resolution No. 11 proposes that Question 15 be deleted in its entirety. Resolution No. 12 requests that the proficiency requirement for the Master Mason
Degree be deleted. It would, however, retain the requirement for the twelvemonth waiting period as previously presented.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes believes that the promise involved in Question 15 as presently written provides the opportunity for a new
Master Mason to acquire additional information and thus become more familiar
with the spirit of Masonry as exemplified in his Lodge. The study and recital of
the Master Mason Degree proficiency continues the valuable education of the
Candidate, as previously accomplished for the Entered Apprentice and Fellow
Craft Degrees, and contributes to his understanding of Freemasonry and its
principles. Without such a comprehension no Brother is likely to be a worthy
applicant for any other body of Masonry.
Your Committee believes that a great deal of encouragement and assistance
should be provided for the newly raised Master Mason to enable him to satisfactorily complete his labors.
We further suggest that most Lodges could, and all Lodges should, utilize the
twelve-month waiting period to better advantage by providing more opportunities for Masonic training and explanation to new Brothers. In this manner we
can direct our attention to the quality of our members and lessen our concern over
the quantity.

(13)
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge F. & A. M. of California:

WHEREAS, often a Master receives information from a non-member of his
Lodge indicating that an individual applying for the degrees in his Lodge may indeed be unworthy of becoming a member of the Fraternity, and
WHEREAS, the wording of Section 540 of the California Masonic Code
leads the Master to believe that he cannot or should not give any countenance to
an objection made by one other than a member of his Lodge, and
WHEREAS, such misinterpretation of the true intent of Section 540 in many
cases leads the Master to ignore information which could possibly save future
embarrassment to his Lodge and to Masonry by refusing admission to an unworthy candidate.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, that a new section be added to the
California Masonic Code numbered 540.1, which section shall read as follows:
540. l "OBJECTION BEFORE BALLOT BY NON-MEMBER. A Lodge or
its Master must give immediate attention to an objection made by another Lodge,
any worthy Mason or any other person to the election of an applicant for the
degrees.
The Junior Warden of the Lodge should make an objection on the basis of the
information received, and the Master should appoint a committee to investigate
and report on the validity of the charge. If said committee should determine that
the objection is not a proper or valid one, the Junior Warden shall immediately
withdraw the objection."
Respectfully submitted,
H. DoUGl.AS LEMONS, P.M., No. 699
Referred to the Committees on Jurisprudence and on Policy and General
Purposes:
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:
By Resolution 13 the Grand Lecturer seeks to clarify Section 540 of the
C.M.C. as to who may object to the election of an applicant for the degrees of
Masonry.
Section 540 now states that "objection ... may be made ... by any member
of the Lodge." Many Masters of Lodges interpret this to mean that credence may
be given to and action taken upon only those objections made by members of the
applicant's Lodge.
It would seem to your Committee on Policy and General Purposes that the
Master of a Lodge is duty bound to be as well informed concerning applicants to
his Lodge as is possible. Thus, should any Mason, whether or not a member of
the applicant's Lodge, or a non-Mason, express doubt to the Master as to a
candidate's character or reveal information to the Master which creates such
doubt in the Master's mind, then the Master, himself, under present law can and
should lodge an objection to a ballot being taken.

REPORT ON CONSTRUCTION OF
SECTION 324.2 of CALIFORNIA MASONIC CODE
At the time Section 324.2 was presented to Grand Lodge in 1968 the Committee on Policy and General Purposes felt that the proposed Resolution should be
expanded and accordingly ~-wrote the Section and discussed it with representatives of the proponents and the Committee on Jurisprudence.
The original Section as rewritten by the Committee on Policy and General
Purposes used the words "may be used or served" in lines 5 and 8 of the Section

232

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

as it appears in the California Masonic Code, but after a discussion with representatives of the proponents and the Committee on Jurisprudence the words
"used or" were deleted from line 8. This deletion was made after it was pointed
out that at the 1966 Communication of Grand Lodge Annotations l 99b, l 99c,
l 99f, l 99i and l 99k which prohibited the use of liquor had been repealed and
deleted (See P. 225 of the Proceedings) and that Annotation 199g had been
adopted in 1957 permitting the holding of social meetings in a building where liquor was sold over a bar and that some organizations requiring Masonic affiliation for membership maintained club rooms which were separated from other
business or meeting places in buildings owned by them and in which members
maintained lockers where they kept liquor they used to have a drink before
a dinner after which they would be working. It was felt it was much better to
allow these club rooms and the use (but not the serving) of liquor therein as
above stated than to require that those who were meeting and having dinner in
these club rooms go out to a nearby bar for a drink, recognizing that it is an
American custom and practice to have a drink before dinner. In other words, it
was felt that it is much .better to drink at home than to go out t<? a bar to get a
drink.
It is hoped that this explanation will clarify the meaning of Section 324.2.
Incidentally, it might be noted that when the line was drawn as to treating Masonic Temples and other Masonic buildings alike Grand Lodge refused to adopt
legislation treating them all alike. (1967 Proceedings P. 214) .
Respectfully submitted,
THEODORE MERIAM, Chairman of Committee on
Policy and General Purposes
LEO E. AANDERSON, Chairman of Committee on Jurisprudence
I move that the foregoing be received and placed in the proceedings and that
the Code Commission be instructed to place a note following Section 324.2
referring to this report.
Adopted 5/6 Vote .

Announcement was made of the following appointments by the Grand Masterelect:
As Trustees of the Masonic Homes of California the reappointment of John
M. Faulkner, Raymond Howe and Bus Orear, and the appointment of Past Grand
Master Raymond A. Ebbage and Stephen Collins to fill vacancies on the Board,
including that of Past Grand Master Myron E. Smith whose resignation was
occasioned by his moving out of state.

Grand Lodge was called on at 9:30 A.M., the Grand Master presiding . Worshipful Brother G. K. Rodgers, Master of Silver Gate Lodge No. 296 raised
Grand Lodge. The Grand Chaplain delivered the Invocation.
The minutes of the morning and afternoon sessions of Wednesday , October
16th were read and approved.
NOTE: Grand Lodge considered and acted upon the Grand Master's recommendations (see " Action by Grand Lodge, " following the Grand Master's
Message).

ANNUAL ELECTION
The Grand Master announced that the hour had arrived for the Annual Election
and directed the Grand Secretary to read the sections of the Constitution applying
thereto.
The R.·.W.·.Burton Meyer, Jr., Golden State Lodge No . 358 , was elected
Grand Master.
The R. · W. ·John F. Roberts , Jr., Palo Alto Lodge No. 346 was elected Deputy
Grand Master.
The R. ·. W. · .Kermit A. Jacobson, Cannelita Lodge No. 599, was elected Senior Warden.
The W. Donald B. McCaw , Park-Crockett Lodge No. 139, was elected Junior
Grand Warden.
The M. · .W. ·.Chester R. MacPhee, Past Grand Master, Golden West Lodge
No. 455, was reelected Grand Treasurer.
The M. · .W. ·.Edward H. Siems, Past Grand Master, Plymouth Lodge No.
560, was reelected Grand Secretary.
The V. · .W. · .H. Douglas Lemons, Bixby Knolls Lodge No. 699, was
reelected Grand Lecturer.
The Grand Master-elect announced the names of the appointive officers as
follows :
Grand Chaplain, Roland R. Bach, Service Lodge No . 594.
Assistant Grand Lecturers: Burton 0. Young, Fruitvale Lodge No. 336;
Edward E. Seagle, Polaris Lodge No. 730; Ulysses G. Partopulos, King
Solomon's Seaport Lodge No. 260; Vernon L. Gordon, Joppa Lodge No. 508;
George W. Perkins, Mizpah Lodge No. 378; Ernest W. Newton, Silver Gate
Lodge No. 296.
Grand Orator, Donald Ingalls, North Hollywood Lodge No . 542.
Assistant Grand Treasurer, Louis D. Callison, Vacaville Lodge No. 134.
Assistant Grand Secretary, Verne W. Hendrix, Mount Diablo Lodge No. 448.
Grand Marshal, Thomas J. McKimson , Melrose Lodge No. 602 .
Grand Standard Bearer, James H. Tanaka, Channel Lodge No. 757.
Grand Sword Bearer, Harry L. Hibler, Azure Lodge No . 533 .

NOTE: Following their installation it was reported that R. · .W. ·.John F.
Roberts, Deputy Grand Master; R. · .W. ·.Kermit A. Jacobson, Sr. Grand Warden; and R. · . W. · .Donald B. McCaw, Junior Grand Warden, by virtue of their offices are members of the Board of Trustees of the Masonic Homes .
As Trustee of the California Masonic Memorial Temple, the appointment of
John F. Roberts in lieu of Burton Meyer, Jr.
Grand Lodge was then called off for the purpose of admitting Masons and
friends to witness the second ''open'' installation of Grand Lodge Officers in the
history of this Grand Lodge.

INSTALLATION OF OFFICERS
Most Worshipful William H. Price, Past Grand Master, acted as Master of Ceremonies, and the Officers, elected and appointed, were installed by the retiring
Grand Master in accordance with the Ritual.
The newly installed Grand Master introduced members of his own Lodge and
their ladies present in Grand Lodge, together with his own wife, all of whom were
present in recognition of this singular honor. He then called upon the group assembled who accorded a respect by a standing ovation to a number of guests visiting
from our home for adults at Union City.
Retiring Grand Master Ebbage then presented the Grand Master's lapel pin to
newly installed Grand Master Meyer, and other Officers exchanged the Arthur S.
Crites lapel pins.
Past Grand Master Theodore Meriam presented to Junior Past Grand Master
Ebbage a Past Grand Master' s apron, and in tum Past Grand Master Myron E.
Smith presented to him also a Past Grand Master's certificate which evidenced his
having served as Grand Master.

242

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

Past Grand Master Edward H. Siems presented the retiring Grand Master with
the Past Grand Master's lapel pin as an evidence of appreciation of the Fraternity
for the services which the Grand Master had rendered during his term in office.
Most Worshipful Chester R. MacPhee, Grand Treasurer, presented to Past
Grand Master Ebbage for his wife, a gift from the members of Grand Lodge. Most
Worshipful Raymond Ebbage on her behalf expressed appreciation for the
thoughtfulness.
Newly installed Deputy Grand Master John F. Roberts acknowledged his new
responsibilities with humility and introduced a member of his Lodge who in tum
presented a beautiful hand-crafted gavel to newly installed Grand Master Burton
Meyer, Jr.
Following proclamation of installation, newly installed Grand Master Burton
Meyer, Jr. expressed his appreciation for the thoughtfulness behind the presentation of the gavel, his humility on having been installed and expressed appreciation
to the Brethren for having been elected to this high Masonic office. His expression
of committment for their confidence and his pledge for devoted service to the
Fraternity was received with standing ovation by the Brethren and friends. He then
introduced a large number of friends and Brethren who had travelled from throughout the Jurisdiction to witness the installation.
At 1:45 P.M. all business being completed, Grand Lodge closed in due form.

1 - Summary of Significant
Accounting Policies
The more important accounting policies are summarized
as follows:
Basis of Accounting
The financial statements are presented on the cash
basis of accounting. Generally, revenues are
recorded at the time of receipt and expenses are
recorded when paid.
Investments
Investments in securities purchased are carried
at cost and securities received by gift or bequest
are carried at approximate market value on the
date received.

.

Furniture, Equipment,
and Improvements
At the 1957 Annual Communication, the Grand Lodge
approved the policy of capitalizing amounts
expended for furnishings and equipment after
June 30, 1957· No depreciation is provided on
these assets.
Pension Plan
The Grand Lodge contributes to the California
Masonic Retirement Plan for the benefit of
substantially all full-time employees. Total
pension expense for the years ended June 30, 1974
and 1973 was $7,875 and $7,808, respectively. All
prior and current service costs have been funded.
Assets held by the Fund at December 31, 1973 were
in excess of vested benefits.
Federal and State Income Taxes
The Grand Lodge is exempt from Federal and state
income taxes.

MASONIC HOMES OF CALIFORNIA
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

265

MASONIC HOMES OF CALIFORNIA
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30 1974 and 1973

June 30, 1974 and 1973
Reserves for
Special Purposes
1 - Summary Of
Accounting Policies
Basis of Accounting
The financial statements are stated on a modified
cash basis of accounting. Generally, revenues
are recorded at the time of receipt and expenses
are recorded when paid. (See Note 3 for changes
in basis of accounting during current year.)
Investments
Investments in securities purchased are carried
at cost and securities received by gift or
bequest are carried at approximate market value
on the date received.

The trustees have established various special
reserves to which are added gifts and bequests
and other amounts which generally are used at
the direction of the trustees for purposes other
than direct operating expenses. The assets
represented by these reserves are included in
the assets of the General Fund.
Pensions
The Homes contributes to the California Masonic
Retirement Plan for the benefit of substantially
all full-time employees. The total pension
expense for the years ended June 30, 1974 and
1973 was approximately $72,000 and $71,000,
respectively. All prior service and current
service costs have been funded. Assets held by
fund at December 31, 1973 were in excess of
vested benefits.

Other Assets
Other assets consist of life insurance policies,
real estate, and mineral rights assigned or
bequeathed to the Homes. These assets are
recorded at the nominal value of $1 each for
accountability. Payments by the Homes of
obligations of the assignors secured by these
assets are added to the nominal value, with the
exception of life insurance premiums which are
charged to expense when paid.
Property
Land, buildings, and equipment are recorded at
original cost and no depreciation is taken.
Additions which represent minor replacements of
property are charged to expense.

Federal and
State Taxes on Income
The Homes is exempt from Federal and state taxes
on income.

2 - Notes Receivable
Notes receivable arise from the sale of real estate
assigned to the Homes by residents of Decato and from real estate
received as gifts or bequests by Homes.

3 - Change In
Accounting Method
During the year ended June 30, 1974, the Homes changed their
method of accounting for expenditures from accrual to the cash basis
for expenses other than payroll. The effect of this change is an
increase in the excess of revenues collected over expenditures paid
for the year ended June 30, 1974 in the amount of $75,800. The
financial statements for the preceding year have not been restated
for the effects of this change.

266

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

MASONIC HOMES OF CALIFORNIA
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30, 1974 and 1973
4 - Restrictions On Trust Funds
John and Lena Luckenbach Fund
The principal of this fund, restricted by the terms
of the Will of the donor, is to be kept intact and the
income used only for the benefit of the care of orphans
or the aged in Masonic Homes of Southern California.
George F and Laura E Brigham Scholarship Fund
The principal of this fund is held as a Scholarship Fund
for the benefit of the Covina Home residents, of which
$25, 000 may be loaned for this purpose. Income of this
fund is restricted and may be used only for providing
scholarships.
Walter W Schultz and Maude S Schultz Scholarship Fund
The income from this fund is restricted and may be used
only to provide financial assistance to needy children
for educational purposes.
Mildred R Brown and Leroy G Brown Memorial Fund
Principal and income from this fund is to be used for
making loans for educational purposes to any children
that the Board of Trustees deems worthy.
Frederick E and Frieda E Sommers Trust
This fund is to be used exclusively for the education
of full orphan children.
George M and Florence G Perine Endowment Fund
The principal of this fund, subject to the provision
included in the Will of the donor, shall be kept
intact and only the income therefrom shall be used
for the benefit of the Decoto Home.
Harriet C Wadleigh Endowment Annuity Fund
This fund, in the original amount of $3 0 ,000 , is
subject to a contract with the donor providing for the
payment of certain life annuities out of the principal
and income thereof. Under the terms of the contract,
principal of the fund expended in payment of the
annuities is to be later restored out of income when
the annuities no longer absorb the entire income.
After restoration of the principal to the original sum
of $30,000 , the income from the fund is to be used for
the benefit of the residents of the Covina Home.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

MASONIC HOMES OF CALIFORNIA
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30, 1974 and 1973
Student Aid Fund
This fund is designated by the trustees for use for
student aid.
Florence Katherine Burt Trust Fund
The principal of this fund, subject to the provision
in the Will of the donor, was to be used for
renovating present premises or making permanent
additions to the Masonic Homes within a period of
ten years from January 5, 1965, the date of the
decree of distribution. One third of the principal
was designated for the Covina Home and two-thirds
for the Decoto Home. The assets were expended for
the designated purposes, and the fund was closed
during the current year.
Edmund Clement Atkinson Fund
The principal of this fund, subject to the provision
in the Will of the donor, shall be used to contribute
to comfort, convenience, and enjoyment of the
residents of the Decato Home.
Alida o•Meserve Trust Fund
The principal of this fund is to be used for
playgrounds, playground equipment, and other
comparable forms of amusement for the boys at Covina.
Minnie E Peterson Fund
The principal of this fund is held by the Homes
subject to a life annuity.
Ralph Walter Kanz and Russell Joseph Kanz Trusts
The principal and income of these trusts shall be
used for the education of the two named beneficiaries,
subject to the discretion of the trustees. When both
beneficiaries have completed or abandoned their
education or reached age 27, the trust estate
remaining shall be distributed to the Masonic Homes
of California.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

CALIFORNIA MASONIC
MEMORIAL TEMPLE
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30, 1974 and 1973

CALIFORNIA MASONIC
MEMORIAL TEMPLE
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30, 1974 and 1973

3 - Special Feasibility Study

Federal and State Income Taxes

A special feasibility study authorized at the 1971
annual communication was completed at a total cost of $54,500.
Of this amount, $39,500 was charged to expense in the year ended
June 30, 1973 and $15,000, which is recoverable if the same
architect is engaged for continuance of the project, is carried
on the balance sheet as a deposit.

The Temple is exempt from Federal and state
income taxes.
Pension Plan
The Temple contributes to the California Masonic
Retirement Plan for the benefit of substantially
all full-time employees. Total pension expense
was $1,200 in 1974 and 1973. All prior and
current service costs have been funded. Assets
held by the Fund at December ,31, 1973 were in
excess of vested benefits.

CALIFORNIA MASONIC FOUNDATION
NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS
June 30, 1974 and 1973

4 - Amaranth Fund
During 1972 the Foundation received $115,000 in cash
and was assigned a promissory note, secured by a deed of trust,
for $102,791 from the Amaranth Homes of California. The use of
these funds is restricted by a trust agreement with the Amaranth
Homes of California which specifies that the principal is to be
invested and that the income is to be used to provide educational
grants to women under age 21.
